story_type: giant rift across an Antarctic ice shelf, iceberg breaks off
hook: A crack 70 miles long, cutting through Antarctic ice.
narration: This crack in Antarctica was seventy miles long, and it cut right through the ice shelf beneath it.
NASA's Operation IceBridge flew over it and measured it: more than three hundred feet wide, and about a third of a mile deep.
An ice shelf is the floating edge of a glacier. It holds back the ice behind it, like a brake.
Next door, a smaller shelf had fallen apart in 2002, after a rift like this one.
[short pause] The crack had not yet reached all the way across. Once it did, a giant iceberg would break free.
outcome: In July 2017 it broke through, and an iceberg about the size of Delaware split away from the Larsen C ice shelf.
title: A 70-mile crack in Antarctic ice
description:
NASA's Operation IceBridge flew over a massive rift in Antarctica's Larsen C Ice Shelf in 2016 and measured it at about 70 miles long. In July 2017 an iceberg about the size of Delaware split off the shelf.

Footage: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/GSFC_20161208_IceBridge_m12449_IceBridge

facts.claim: Neighbor shelf disintegrated in 2002 after a similar rift
facts.source_quote: Larsen C neighbors a smaller ice shelf that disintegrated in 2002 after developing a rift similar to the one now growing in Larsen C.

facts.claim: Delaware-size iceberg split off between July 10 and 12 (2017 release)
